claim: *Three views of the control machinery.* The catalogue identifies controls; the interaction view relates controls through shared resources; the coverage view relates controls to the obligations that justify them. Stable identities connect the three views while letting each answer a different engineering question. A missing mechanism appears as a coverage gap; an untraced mechanism appears as a candidate orphan.
topology: Three panels retain common A/B/C identities; interaction A/B collide, C isolated; coverage gap and orphan are unlinked.
required_terms: Stable identities join three views; each answers a different engineering question.
bw_encoding: Stable control identities share shading across all views; dashed missing coverage and orphan controls remain visibly exceptional. All strokes and fills are neutral grayscale; labels remain the primary semantic key. Existing dashed meanings are preserved.
redesign: Native nodes and routed edges preserve the original semantic structure, with print-sized labels and fewer decorative frames. Grayscale refinement: Stable control identities share shading across all views; dashed missing coverage and orphan controls remain visibly exceptional. Fidelity pass: Routed dashed bidirectional conflict edge above controls so the dash pattern is visible instead of collapsing into two touching arrowheads.
alt:
Three panels over the same three controls, carried by stable identities: [A] squash rule,
    [B] brief guard, [C] lint gate. Left panel, the catalogue, lists the three controls that exist. Middle
    panel, the interaction graph, relates [A] and [B] through a shared resource, the commit set, where they
    collide; [C] stands alone. Right panel, the coverage view, relates controls to the obligations that
    justify them: scope-bounded traces to [A] and brief-followed to [B], while the cost-ceiling obligation
    has no control — a coverage gap — and [C] traces to no obligation — an orphan. The same control identities appear in every view; each view selects and adds the
    relations its engineering question needs.
